questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people are reading fewer books
How to teach children to read faster
How learning to read changes the brain
The history of the world's longest novels
questions.why: They hear experts explain how reading changes our brains, and how different languages shape them.

questions.q: Why does Georgie usually read before bed?
options: It's the only time her house is quiet
She reads books for work
Her doctor told her to
It helps her relax and fall asleep
questions.why: She says she reads before bed because it helps her relax and go to sleep.

questions.q: What is Maryanne Wolf's view of reading?
options: It is just as natural for humans as speaking
It is not natural at all, unlike spoken language
Children learn it easily without any help
It is much easier than learning to speak
questions.why: She says we think reading must be natural because language is, 'But it isn't.'

questions.q: According to scientific studies, what networks are we born with?
options: Ones for seeing and making sounds, not for reading
Ones for reading and writing from the very start
Ones for all the skills we will ever need in life
Only ones for hearing and understanding voices
questions.why: Becca says our brains have networks for seeing and producing sounds, but not the pathways to read.

questions.q: According to Rebecca Gotlieb, how does the brain manage to read?
options: It uses one small part of the brain that grows
It stops using the parts that are used for vision
It relies only on memory of words we have seen
It borrows parts used for vision, sound and attention
questions.why: She says we co-opt parts of the brain involved in vision, auditory processing, language, attention and affect.

questions.q: What does Rebecca say happens when we develop a reading brain?
options: Only our eyesight improves as we read more
The brain's activity, structure and links change
The brain slowly becomes smaller with age
Nothing in the brain changes after childhood
questions.why: She says it alters everything, from brain activity to brain structure and connectivity.

questions.q: What does research suggest about reading Chinese characters?
options: It uses exactly the same brain areas as reading English
It is impossible for English speakers
It activates different brain areas from reading an alphabet
It only uses the parts of the brain for sound
questions.why: Becca says learning these symbols activates different areas of the brain from alphabet-based systems.

questions.q: Why do the presenters mention the bilingual man who had a stroke?
options: To show Chinese and English use different circuits
To show that strokes can sometimes improve reading
To explain why English is easier than Chinese
To warn about the dangers of reading too much
questions.why: After the stroke he couldn't read Chinese but could still read English, showing different circuits.
